definition: Disparage means to criticize or speak ill of someone or something; to belittle or put it down.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word disparage. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know disparage should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The head chef would often disparage frozen vegetables, insisting that no serious kitchen should ever rely on them.
To criticize is simply to point out faults, but to disparage adds a dismissive, belittling tone that treats the target as unworthy of respect.
To disparage is to belittle, while to vilify goes much further and paints someone as truly evil or hateful.

To belittle is to make something seem smaller and less important than it really is - waving off a hard-won achievement as easy. To disparage is the broader formal word for talking something down, and belittling is its favorite method. Every belittling remark disparages; disparage also covers sneers, put-downs, and dismissals of every kind.

To demean is to attack dignity - to treat a person as beneath respect, lowering their standing. To disparage is to talk down the worth of things as readily as people: a chef can disparage frozen vegetables all day. You demean only people; you can disparage a person, a method, or a product.

To ridicule is to make someone or something an object of mocking laughter - the weapon is the joke. To disparage needs no humor at all: a flat dismissal of something as worthless disparages without a single laugh. Ridicule wants an audience laughing; disparaging just wants the target diminished.

Disparage means to criticize or speak ill of someone or something; to belittle or put it down.
At the community garden, Rosa listened politely as a longtime member continued to disparage store-bought compost, calling it lifeless dirt in a fancy bag.
Rosa had used it successfully for years, so she simply smiled and kept planting.
The longtime member is not offering helpful advice; he is belittling the compost and dismissing it as worthless, which is exactly what it means to disparage something.
Disparage is a formal word for belittling criticism.
Use it when someone talks down about a person or thing, not when they simply disagree; you can disagree respectfully, but you cannot disparage respectfully.

disparage: To disparage is to belittle, while to vilify goes much further and paints someone as truly evil or hateful.
For thirty years, the director Elena Vargas has been famous for two things: her prize-winning films and her sharp tongue.
In nearly every interview she finds a way to disparage streaming movies, dismissing the entire format as disposable work.
Critics note that she never jokes about it and never singles out one filmmaker; her scorn lands on the format itself.
Last spring, however, a reporter discovered that Vargas had quietly financed two streaming features under another name.
Asked about the contradiction, she shrugged: even a form she talks down, she said, can pay for the films she loves.
